key_insight: Chronological pre-training creates "specialist" models that update new knowledge much faster than randomly ordered "generalist" models, while still preserving useful historical knowledge.
engineering_relevance: For continual learning and model maintenance, how you order pre-training data can materially reduce future update cost and improve adaptability without redesigning the update algorithm.
method: Compare models pretrained on chronologically ordered vs randomly shuffled time-varying knowledge.
Measure how many update steps are needed to acquire new knowledge after pre-training.
Derive a first-principles law linking update cost to optimization dynamics, then use it to guide data-organization strategy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports empirical results showing specialists require far fewer update steps than generalists, and that the derived law closely predicts these update costs across experiments and real-world pretrained models.
watch_item: The benefits depend on temporal structure in the data, so gains may be smaller or harder to realize when knowledge is not naturally time-ordered or when reordering pre-training data is impractical.
paper_title: Specialists Learn Faster: Knowledge Organization in Pre-training Shapes Knowledge Update Efficiency
